title: Patient-Reported Outcomes In Performance Measurement
abstract: Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are measures of how patients feel or what they are able to do in the context of their health status; PROs are reports, usually on questionnaires, about a patient's health conditions, health behaviors, or experiences with health care that individuals report directly, without modification of responses by clinicians or others; thus, they directly reflect the voice of the patient. PROs cover domains such as physical health, mental and emotional health, functioning, symptoms and symptom burden, and health behaviors. They are relevant for many activities: helping patients and their clinicians make informed decisions about health care, monitoring the progress of care, setting policies for coverage and reimbursement of health services, improving the quality of health care services, and tracking or reporting on the performance of health care delivery organizations. We address the major methodological issues related to choosing, administering, and using PROs for these purposes, particularly in clinical practice settings. We include a framework for best practices in selecting PROs, focusing on choosing appropriate methods and modes for administering PRO measures to accommodate patients with diverse linguistic, cultural, educational, and functional skills, understanding measures developed through both classic and modern test theory, and addressing complex issues relating to scoring and analyzing PRO data.

narrative:
Short impact summary

Patient-Reported Outcomes In Performance Measurement (2015), published by RTI Press, has been cited 333 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 10% of works in its field and year.

Full narrative

Patient-Reported Outcomes In Performance Measurement by David Cella, Elizabeth Hahn, Sally Jensen and others was published by RTI Press in 2015. Conceptually, the work connects to Reimbursement, Health care, Context (archaeology), Mental health and Medicine.

OpenAlex records 333 citations. That places it in the top 10% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2023 with 37 citing works. Notable citing venues include Quality of Life Research, Journal of Patient-Reported Outcomes and Research Square. Of 268 citation statements scite has classified, 1 support its claims, 267 mention it in passing, and none contradict it. The citing works include 211 journal articles, 26 reviews, 13 preprints and 11 book chapters. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada.

Its subject matter aligns with Quality Education among the Sustainable Development Goals.
